title: Fictional map digitization: conditions and clocks

input.text:
Aurora Map Digitization Desk is an invented service for this closed-world test. Use only the following rules; they are not real service policy.
Intake and batch size: a batch contains at most 5 paper map sheets. Customer upload of a request is not the intake event. Intake occurs when an operator scans the batch ticket.
Inspection clock: the format inspection must finish within 16 minutes after that operator scan. This inspection window is not a promise that the output is ready in 16 minutes.
Release and retention: output may be released only after BOTH the map review and the output checksum check have passed. Passing just one check is insufficient. A failed checksum blocks release. The 36-hour output-retention window starts when the checksum check passes, even if map review is still pending; it does not start at the request, intake, or first download. Downloading does not restart this window.
Retention clock: once that 36-hour window ends, the stored output is deleted. The brief defines no extension, recovery, retry process, fee, rush option, scanning resolution, opening hours, location, calendar date, or handling of a job whose map review remains pending at deletion. Preserve these gaps rather than promising an outcome. Explain a deeper branch through the conditions and clocks without inventing a customer's case.

fact_checks.claim: The maximum is 5 paper map sheets per batch; it is neither a minimum nor a daily limit.
fact_checks.evidence_excerpt: a batch contains at most 5 paper map sheets

fact_checks.claim: The 16-minute inspection window starts at the operator scan and is not an output-ready promise.
fact_checks.evidence_excerpt: the format inspection must finish within 16 minutes after that operator scan. This inspection window is not a promise that the output is ready in 16 minutes.

fact_checks.claim: Release requires both map review and checksum check to pass; either alone is insufficient.
fact_checks.evidence_excerpt: output may be released only after BOTH the map review and the output checksum check have passed. Passing just one check is insufficient.

fact_checks.claim: The 36-hour window starts on checksum pass even while review is pending, and download does not reset it.
fact_checks.evidence_excerpt: The 36-hour output-retention window starts when the checksum check passes, even if map review is still pending; it does not start at the request, intake, or first download. Downloading does not restart this window.

fact_checks.claim: Stored output is deleted at the end of the retention window rather than kept permanently.
fact_checks.evidence_excerpt: once that 36-hour window ends, the stored output is deleted.

forbidden_claims.claim: Output release is guaranteed within 16 minutes.
forbidden_claims.reason: This turns an inspection deadline into a delivery guarantee.

forbidden_claims.claim: The 36 hours start only after both checks pass or after first download.
forbidden_claims.reason: The retention clock is independently anchored to checksum pass.

forbidden_claims.claim: Passing either check permits release, or a failed checksum still permits release.
forbidden_claims.reason: This breaks the conjunction and failed-check gate.

forbidden_claims.claim: Deleted outputs are guaranteed recoverable, or pending review automatically extends retention.
forbidden_claims.reason: Recovery, extensions, and the pending-review outcome are undefined.

unknown_limits: Extensions, recovery, retries, fees, rush processing, resolution, hours, location, dates, and the disposition of a job still awaiting review at deletion.
